body.en: The integral is the second fundamental question of calculus: how continuous quantities accumulate over space and time. Geometrically, the definite integral measures the net signed area bounded between a curve and the horizontal coordinate axis.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Riemann Sum Formulations & Limits of Partitions

body.en: Integral calculus transforms discrete approximations into exact continuous accumulation through the limit of Riemann sums over arbitrarily fine partitions.

A partition \( P \) of \( [a, b] \) is a finite ordered set \( a = x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_n = b \). The width of the \( i \)-th subinterval is \( \Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1} \), and the partition norm is \( \|P\| = \max_{1 \le i \le n} \Delta x_i \).

Choosing sample points \( x_i^* \in [x_{i-1}, x_i] \), the Riemann sum is: \[ S(f, P) = \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x_i. \] If \( S(f, P) \) approaches a finite number \( I \) as \( \|P\| \to 0 \) regardless of partition or sample choices, \( f \) is Riemann integrable on \( [a, b] \), written: \[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \lim_{\|P\| \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)\,\Delta x_i. \]

label.en: ● Theorem & Uniform Sum Formula · Integrability of Continuous Functions

body.en: Theorem: Every continuous function on a closed bounded interval \( [a, b] \) is Riemann integrable. Furthermore, using a regular partition into \( n \) subintervals of uniform width \( \Delta x = \frac{b-a}{n} \) with right-endpoint evaluation \( x_i = a + i\Delta x \): \[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f\left(a + i\frac{b-a}{n}\right)\frac{b-a}{n}. \quad \blacksquare \]

blocks.heading: Fundamental properties of the definite integral

label.en: Level 1 (Foundations) — Worked Example · Computing an Integral Directly via Riemann Sum Limit

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate \( \displaystyle \int_0^3 (2x + 1)\,dx \) using the formal limit definition of a Riemann sum with uniform right endpoints.

Step 1 · Setup Partition: With \( [a, b] = [0, 3] \): \[ \Delta x = \frac{3 - 0}{n} = \frac{3}{n}, \qquad x_i = a + i\Delta x = 0 + i\left(\frac{3}{n}\right) = \frac{3i}{n}. \]

Step 2 · Form the Riemann Sum: \[ f(x_i) = 2\left(\frac{3i}{n}\right) + 1 = \frac{6i}{n} + 1. \] \[ S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i)\,\Delta x = \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{6i}{n} + 1\right)\frac{3}{n} = \frac{18}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n i + \frac{3}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n 1. \]

Step 3 · Substitute Power Sum Formulas: Using \( \sum_{i=1}^n i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} \) and \( \sum_{i=1}^n 1 = n \): \[ S_n = \frac{18}{n^2} \cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + \frac{3}{n}(n) = 9\left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right) + 3 = 12 + \frac{9}{n}. \]

Step 4 · Evaluate Limit as \( n \to \infty \): \[ \int_0^3 (2x + 1)\,dx = \lim_{n\to\infty}\left(12 + \frac{9}{n}\right) = 12 + 0 = \mathbf{12}. \]

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Express the infinite summation limit as a definite integral on the interval \( [0, 1] \) and evaluate it: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{i^3}{n^4}. \]

solution.en: Factor \( \frac{1}{n} = \Delta x \): \[ \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{i^3}{n^4} = \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{1}{n}. \] Here \( x_i = \frac{i}{n} = 0 + i\Delta x \) with \( \Delta x = \frac{1}{n} \), matching the right Riemann sum of \( f(x) = x^3 \) on \( [0, 1] \): \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^3 \frac{1}{n} = \int_0^1 x^3\,dx = \left[ \frac{x^4}{4} \right]_0^1 = \frac{1^4}{4} - 0 = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Left, Right, Midpoint & Trapezoidal Approximations with Concavity Bounds

body.en: In real-world applications where antiderivatives lack elementary formulas or data comes from discrete sensors, numerical approximations provide controlled estimates with precise error bounds.

label.en: ● Theorem & Error Bounds · Numerical Approximations & Over/Underestimate Criteria

body.en:
Overestimate / Underestimate Criteria:

  • Monotonicity: If \( f'(x) > 0 \) (strictly increasing), then \( L_n < \int_a^b f(x)\,dx < R_n \). If \( f'(x) < 0 \) (strictly decreasing), then \( R_n < \int_a^b f(x)\,dx < L_n \).
  • Concavity: If \( f''(x) > 0 \) (concave up), chords lie above the curve and mid-tangents lie below, so \( M_n < \int_a^b f(x)\,dx < T_n \). If \( f''(x) < 0 \) (concave down), then \( T_n < \int_a^b f(x)\,dx < M_n \).

Error Bounds: If \( |f''(x)| \le K \) on \( [a, b] \): \[ |E_T| \le \frac{K(b-a)^3}{12n^2}, \qquad |E_M| \le \frac{K(b-a)^3}{24n^2}. \] Notice the Midpoint Rule is twice as accurate as the Trapezoidal Rule for the same number of subintervals.

label.en: Level 2 (Medium) — Worked Example · Non-Uniform Tabular Data Approximations

body.en:
Problem: A velocity telemetry stream \( v(t) \) is sampled at non-uniform intervals:

Time \( t \) (s)025610
Velocity \( v(t) \) (m/s)410161420

Approximate the total distance traveled \( \int_0^{10} v(t)\,dt \) using a Trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals.

Step 1 · Trapezoid Areas with Variable \( \Delta t_i \):
• Subinterval 1 \( [0, 2] \): \( \Delta t_1 = 2 \); Area \( = \frac{4 + 10}{2}(2) = 14 \).
• Subinterval 2 \( [2, 5] \): \( \Delta t_2 = 3 \); Area \( = \frac{10 + 16}{2}(3) = 13 \times 3 = 39 \).
• Subinterval 3 \( [5, 6] \): \( \Delta t_3 = 1 \); Area \( = \frac{16 + 14}{2}(1) = 15 \times 1 = 15 \).
• Subinterval 4 \( [6, 10] \): \( \Delta t_4 = 4 \); Area \( = \frac{14 + 20}{2}(4) = 17 \times 4 = 68 \).

Step 2 · Sum Total Distance: \[ \text{Total Distance} \approx 14 + 39 + 15 + 68 = \mathbf{136 \text{ meters}}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Find the minimum number of subintervals \( n \) required to guarantee that the Trapezoidal approximation of \( \displaystyle \int_1^3 \frac{1}{x}\,dx \) has an absolute error less than \( 10^{-4} \).

solution.en:
Compute second derivative: \( f(x) = x^{-1} \implies f'(x) = -x^{-2} \implies f''(x) = 2x^{-3} = \frac{2}{x^3} \).
On \( [1, 3] \), \( |f''(x)| = \frac{2}{x^3} \) is decreasing, so its maximum occurs at \( x = 1 \): \( K = \frac{2}{1^3} = 2 \).
Using the Trapezoidal error bound with \( a = 1, b = 3 \): \[ |E_T| \le \frac{K(b-a)^3}{12n^2} = \frac{2(3-1)^3}{12n^2} = \frac{2(8)}{12n^2} = \frac{16}{12n^2} = \frac{4}{3n^2}. \] Require: \[ \frac{4}{3n^2} < 10^{-4} \implies n^2 > \frac{4 \times 10^4}{3} = \frac{40000}{3} \approx 13333.33 \implies n > \sqrt{13333.33} \approx 115.47. \] Since \( n \) must be an integer, we require at least \( \mathbf{n = 116} \) subintervals.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Darboux Integrability & The Mean Value Theorem for Definite Integrals

body.en: A fully rigorous treatment of integration establishes the existence of the integral through supremum and infimum bounds on Darboux sums, culminating in the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals.

label.en: ● Theorem & Proof · The Mean Value Theorem for Definite Integrals

body.en:
Theorem (MVT for Integrals): If \( f \) is continuous on the closed interval \( [a, b] \), then there exists at least one number \( c \in [a, b] \) such that: \[ f(c) = \frac{1}{b - a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx, \qquad \text{or equivalently: } \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = f(c)(b - a). \]

Proof: Since \( f \) is continuous on \( [a, b] \), by the Extreme Value Theorem \( f \) attains an absolute minimum \( m \) and absolute maximum \( M \) on \( [a, b] \): \[ m \le f(x) \le M \quad \forall x \in [a, b]. \] Integrating across \( [a, b] \): \[ \int_a^b m\,dx \le \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \le \int_a^b M\,dx \implies m(b - a) \le \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \le M(b - a). \] Dividing by \( (b - a) > 0 \): \[ m \le \frac{1}{b - a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \le M. \] By the Intermediate Value Theorem, since \( f \) is continuous on \( [a, b] \), \( f \) must take on every value between its minimum \( m \) and maximum \( M \). Therefore, there exists some \( c \in [a, b] \) such that \( f(c) = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \). \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced) — Worked Example · Average Value & Finding Certified MVT Coordinates

body.en:
Problem: For \( f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x + 1 \) on \( [0, 2] \), calculate the exact average value \( f_{\text{avg}} \), and determine all certified values \( c \in [0, 2] \) guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals.

Step 1 · Compute Definite Integral: \[ \int_0^2 (3x^2 - 2x + 1)\,dx = \left[ x^3 - x^2 + x \right]_0^2 = (2^3 - 2^2 + 2) - 0 = (8 - 4 + 2) = 6. \]

Step 2 · Calculate Average Value: \[ f_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{b - a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2 - 0}(6) = \mathbf{3}. \]

Step 3 · Solve for \( c \): Set \( f(c) = f_{\text{avg}} = 3 \): \[ 3c^2 - 2c + 1 = 3 \implies 3c^2 - 2c - 2 = 0. \] By the quadratic formula: \[ c = \frac{-(-2) \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(3)(-2)}}{2(3)} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 24}}{6} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{28}}{6} = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{7}}{3}. \] Evaluate values:
• \( c_1 = \frac{1 + \sqrt{7}}{3} \approx \frac{1 + 2.646}{3} = 1.215 \in [0, 2] \) (Valid!).
• \( c_2 = \frac{1 - \sqrt{7}}{3} \approx \frac{1 - 2.646}{3} = -0.549 \notin [0, 2] \) (Outside interval).
Therefore, the unique certified value is \( \mathbf{c = \frac{1 + \sqrt{7}}{3}} \).

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the definite integral analytically: \[ \int_{-3}^3 \left( x^5 \sqrt{9 - x^2} + \sqrt{9 - x^2} \right) dx. \]

solution.en: Split the integral using linearity: \[ \int_{-3}^3 x^5 \sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx + \int_{-3}^3 \sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx. \] Part 1 · Symmetry Analysis: Let \( g(x) = x^5 \sqrt{9 - x^2} \). Then \( g(-x) = (-x)^5 \sqrt{9 - (-x)^2} = -x^5 \sqrt{9 - x^2} = -g(x) \). Because \( g \) is an odd function integrated over symmetric limits \([-3, 3]\): \[ \int_{-3}^3 x^5 \sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx = 0. \] Part 2 · Geometric Area: The integrand \( y = \sqrt{9 - x^2} \ge 0 \) represents the upper half of the circle \( x^2 + y^2 = 9 \) with radius \( r = 3 \). The integral from \( -3 \) to \( 3 \) is the area of a semicircle: \[ \int_{-3}^3 \sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi (3^2) = \frac{9\pi}{2}. \] Summing both parts: \[ 0 + \frac{9\pi}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{9\pi}{2}}. \]

body.en:
Signed Area vs Total Geometric Area: The definite integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) computes net signed area (regions below the x-axis carry negative weight). If total geometric area is requested, you must integrate the absolute value \(\int_a^b |f(x)|\,dx\), splitting the integral at each x-intercept.

Non-Uniform Partitions: The common formula \(\frac{b-a}{2n}[f(x_0) + 2f(x_1) + \dots + f(x_n)]\) works ONLY for regular uniform intervals. For tabular exam questions with varying time gaps, you MUST calculate each trapezoid area \(\frac{y_i + y_{i+1}}{2}\Delta x_i\) individually.

Over/Underestimate Justifications: Always cite the correct derivative order in exam justifications: increasing/decreasing is governed by the first derivative \(f'\); concave up/down is governed by the second derivative \(f''\).
